Objective: reduce time to a fully gate-passing preview without weakening quality gates, template fidelity, contrast, accessibility, or generated-site performance.

Subtasks: `Eu8VeRyzIx` baseline instrumentation, `urG9LOHFG3` template adherence, `HwcDIM9Z8C` pre-judge checks, `upH1K2ycXr` concurrency, `QoJ1ITZY7e` evidence reuse, `!qkWE8QN6h` progress-aware repairs, `CcWvdWhCi5` matched validation/rollout.

### Phase 1 progress: timing instrumentation (baseline-capable)

- Recon (four read-only subagent maps + direct reads) established the actual critical path: per bakeoff round every non-excluded candidate is re-promoted, re-built, re-contrast-audited, re-captured at 3 viewports + authored pages, and re-judged with ~10 high-detail images; the round loop repairs one candidate per round and re-evaluates everything; the visual gate is a separate child process per round. Round dirs `round-00..10` on the #158 acceptance reflect that loop exhausting budgets.
- New `scripts/creative-timing.mjs`: recorder with `record`/`time`, per-category summaries, structured `launchloomTiming` log line. `scripts/report-creative-timings.mjs`: reads a QA `.launchloom` dir (`pipeline-test-report.json` stages, `creative-repair/timing.json`, per-round bakeoff reports, `repair-usage.json`) and can `--compare` two runs with stage/creative/call deltas.
- Wired durations without behavior change: judge + diversity evaluators now return `durationMs`/`attempts` (whole logical call incl. retries); creative repair usage records gain `durationMs`/`attempts`; bakeoff records per-candidate phase timings (`source`, `promote`, `build`, `contrast`, `capture`, `authored-pages`, `judge`) into `candidate.timings` + `report.timings`; orchestrator writes `creative-repair/timing.json` (bakeoff/gate/repair/entries) and flushes it as entries are recorded so failed runs keep the data.
- Tests: `tests/creative-timing.test.ts` (6), `tests/report-creative-timings.test.ts` (3), new assertions in `tests/rendered-creative-repair.test.ts` (54 passed incl. timing.json entries) and `tests/creative-promotion.test.ts` (bakeoff report timings; full suite 22 passed). Also green: creative-repair-loop, creative-judge-runtime, openrouter-cache-integration (142 tests), generation-cost-summary, inference-client, creative-repair-experiment.
- Next: push this instrumentation commit and dispatch the matched BASELINE creative-only run of intake #158 (`inference_provider=opencode-go`) from this exact SHA; then implement phases 2-6 on top while it runs.

### Baseline dispatch + phases 4/5/6/2 landed (same branch)

- Baseline run `38878871977` dispatched from commit `28ed8952` (instrumentation only) at 09:12Z, `creative-only` intake #158, `inference_provider=opencode-go`, QA repo `WrazyAI/llqa-158-creative-38878871977-1`. It pins its own SHA; later commits do not affect it.
- Evidence reuse (plan phase 5): new `scripts/creative-evidence-cache.mjs` stores per-candidate rendered evidence + judge result keyed on a digest of candidate sources, shared site inputs, render settings, judge model, and a version constant. Managed contrast-correction blocks are stripped before hashing so persisted auto-repairs do not invalidate their own evidence; `.launchloom`, candidate dirs, per-round evidence dirs, and the candidate-derived `selected` directory are excluded from the shared digest; evidence with missing files or failed judges is never reused. The orchestrator enables reuse by default (`CREATIVE_EVIDENCE_REUSE=false` kill-switch) and passes `evidence-cache/` into each bakeoff; on a hit the round restores screenshots into its own evidence dir so repair/gate inputs keep working unchanged. Diversity judging is deliberately NOT cached (always re-evaluated), so a changed member can never inherit an old diversity pass.
- Bounded concurrency (plan phase 4): per-candidate judges are scheduled immediately after that candidate's render and overlap the next candidate's render, bounded by `createTaskLimiter` at 2 workers (env `CREATIVE_JUDGE_CONCURRENCY`, clamped 1-3). The candidate loop now has a post-render pass that merges deferred judge results, writes reusable evidence, then scores; models, reasoning, screenshots, viewports, and candidate count are unchanged.
- Progress-aware repairs (plan phase 6): `blockingFindingsSignature` (sha256 of normalized blocking findings) plus a stagnation guard in `run-rendered-creative-repair.mjs` (`MAX_STAGNANT_REPAIRS = 2`). Repairs that leave the blocking set byte-identical twice mark a candidate stagnated; its remaining budget is not spent, other candidates can still be repaired, and the loop fails with an explicit `Stagnation guard:` error instead of repeating equivalent work. Budget-cap tests now vary blocker text to keep exercising the pure budget path; new tests cover the guard and the deferred-judge wiring.
- Template adherence (plan phase 2): new `scripts/design-adherence-guidance.mjs` reads the retained Apache-2.0 frontend-design review copy from `docs/design-guidance/anthropic/frontend-design/SKILL.md` at runtime (no network fetch; provenance pinned in that directory's README) and pairs it with a binding `TEMPLATE_ADHERENCE_CONTRACT` (preserve structure/section order/mechanics/interactions; adapt copy, brand roles, imagery, responsive composition; prohibit generic substitutions, invented facts, trade-dress copying, and boxed contrast fixes). Both blocks now reach the authoring system prompt and the repair prompt's cached reference context.
- Structural drift detection: `reference-contract-compliance.mjs` now reports a critical `section-order` finding when `data-reference-section` values appear out of the assigned sequence (extra local sections are allowed). Verified against the real acceptance-run candidates (`candidate-a/b/c` from `llqa-158-creative-38620904674-1`): all three already conform and produce zero section findings, so this adds drift detection without retroactively failing conforming work.
- Tests so far: creative-evidence-cache (8), task-limiter (2), creative-timing (6), report-creative-timings (3), design-adherence-guidance (3), reference-fidelity incl. two new order tests, creative-repair-loop 135 across three suites, rendered-creative-repair (56 incl. stagnation + kill-switch), creative-promotion reuse test (4 bakeoffs, 29s, only 3 real renders). Full `npm test` running; fix-forward for any suite that asserted the old bakeoff flow.

### Phase 3 coverage findings + validation matrix

- Cheap-check ordering (plan phase 3) verified as largely pre-existing in `run-creative-bakeoff.mjs` per candidate and before any model call: content-manifest check, source contract validation, promote validation, Astro build, built routes, deterministic contrast audit with foreground-only repairs, composition-topology geometry, viewport captures with required fragment/nav-target checks (`missingFragments`, `missingNavTargets`), broken-image and unnamed-control counts, overflow, and browser-error capture. The judge only runs after these, and missing screenshot files fail inside the evaluator before any model request. Added in this workstream: the deterministic `section-order` drift finding (phase 2) and the documented ordering above. No redundant duplicate check was added.
- `scripts/report-creative-timings.mjs` was validated against the real historical QA evidence (`WrazyAI/llqa-158-creative-38620904674-1`, cloned to /tmp): it reads stage durations, round dirs, and gracefully reports pre-instrumentation runs (no timing.json) without error. Round 08-10 exclude candidate-c, matching the recorded exclusion behavior.
- Matched validation matrix (plan phase 7): baseline runs pinned to `28ed8952` on branch `codex/launchloom-creative-loop-baseline`; optimized runs from the optimization branch. Intakes: #158 Harbor Glow Plumbing (historically difficult, local trades) and #134 Velvet Fern Skin Studio (calm editorial/care). Baseline #158 `38878871977` started 09:12Z; baseline #134 `38882139037` started 09:41Z. Optimized runs dispatch after the full local suite is green so an unvalidated SHA never reaches the comparison.
- Full-suite debugging found and fixed a real race: the debounced `timing.json` write could overlap a concurrent writer and leave a partial file. `persistRunTiming` now serializes writes through a promise chain and lands them via staging file + rename (atomic); the stagnation and budget error paths await a final persist before throwing. Three consecutive `rendered-creative-repair` runs and the complete `npm test` suite are green afterward (130 files, 2193 tests, 0 failed, ~7.5 min).
- Added `CREATIVE_REPAIR_STAGNATION=false` as the third reversible switch (with a test) and `docs/creative-generation-performance.md` documenting the changes, switches, and the analyzer; `npm run report:creative-timings` alias added.

### CodeRabbit review round (local CLI, 4 minor findings, all resolved)

- **Judge-count integrity (major impact on reported numbers):** reused candidates carried `timings.judge`/`judgeCallMs` copied from the cached bundle, so round reports looked like fresh judge calls and the analyzer's fallback path over-counted (it had reported 31 -> 33). Fixes: the render snapshot strips judge timing keys before caching; reuse copies render timings only; `judgeCallMs`/`judgeAttempts` are recorded only when a judge task actually ran this round; and the analyzer now prefers the bakeoff's per-round recorder (`timings.categories`) as the authoritative call count with layered fallbacks. Corrected #158 figures (also posted to the PR): judge calls 31 -> 11, 12.8m -> 6.5m; diversity 11 -> 11, 1.1m -> 0.8m.
- **Analyzer diversity totals:** `diversityMs` now comes from the per-round reports instead of the (never-written) orchestrator timing entries.
- **CLI entry-point check:** `report-creative-timings.mjs` uses `pathToFileURL` so checkouts with spaces still run.
- **Ledger hygiene:** the repository is public; absolute operator paths, usernames, and host-specific credential provenance were replaced with neutral references in this ledger. (Older daily ledgers still contain absolute paths; left untouched as out of scope.)
- Tests updated for all of the above (reused candidates carry no judge timing fields; a retried judge records `judgeCallMs`; analyzer counts come from the per-round recorder; a reused candidate fixture proves it is reported but not counted). Full `creative-promotion` suite (24 tests), analyzer, timing, and repair-loop suites green; `npm run check` reports 0 errors.
- **Second matched pair (#134) complete:** baseline `38928340329` (28ed8952) -> optimized `38928345911` (ecc01626), 3 candidates both sides: total 110.1m -> 74.0m (-33%); creative 81.4m -> 48.5m (-40%); bakeoff 49.8m -> 18.8m (-62%); judge calls 24 -> 8 (7.7m -> 4.0m); diversity 9 -> 5; repairs 15 -> 14 (31.5m -> 29.6m); rounds 11 -> 9; technical gates failed on both sides; verdict failed (creative gate) on both; cost USD 0.371 -> 0.341. **Both runs generated real client imagery (2 routes each), live-validating the rotated FAL key** (same-intake earlier runs produced zero images with `fal-request-failed`). Combined matched-pair evidence: total -30% / -33%, creative -34% / -40%, bakeoff wall -57% / -62%, judge calls -65% / -67%, with gate outcomes identical and no budget weakened. The #134 optimized side ran `ecc01626`; the later `30401245`/`8d3acbf5` fixes (judge accounting, analyzer, exact order gate) are timing/analysis/gate-precision changes that can only reduce false positives, so the measured deltas are conservative-safe.
- **Second review finding (major, fixed in `8d3acbf5`):** the section-order hard gate fed id-only sections (#services/#faqs/#contact) into fuzzy substring matching, so a conversion-first layout could be flagged as drift. The gate now reads only explicit `data-reference-section` values, slug-normalizes them, and requires exact membership in the assigned sequence. Regression test reproduces the reviewer's scenario (moved id-only contact section stays clean), genuine reordering still fails, and all six real candidates from today's baseline+optimized runs produce zero section-order findings. A third CodeRabbit verification pass kept hitting the free-tier rate limit; that limitation is noted for the final report.
